mainTopic: אתנן זונה: when a payment to a זונה is forbidden for the מזבח, and which women and relationships it covers
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי אלעזר's case: a lamb given to a זונה is permitted for the מזבח if she offered it before the ביאה. The גמרא shows this only works when he said the lamb is hers at the ביאה, but hers right away if she needs it. רב אושעיא then asks about a lamb she only made הקדש before the ביאה, and the question ends in תיקו. Next, two ברייתות disagree about payment given after the ביאה. רב חנן בר רב חסדא explains that a specific promised lamb is אתנן, while an unspecified lamb is not. רב and לוי then argue about whether payment to one's own wife who is a נדה counts as אתנן, each relying on a different word in the פסוק. אביי holds that a gentile זונה's payment is forbidden but a Jewish זונה's is permitted, with the opposite result for a כהן's lashes. רבא makes both cases equal. A ברייתא is used to challenge both opinions, and the answer to the last challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The lamb is permitted when she offered it first
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the lamb is permitted when the זונה brought it as a קרבן before the ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where she went ahead and offered the lamb as a קרבן first.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes רבי אלעזר's answer from just before. The lamb is not considered אתנן because she already offered it before the ביאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition of אתנן applies to payment for a ביאה. If the lamb was already offered on the מזבח before any ביאה took place, it was never payment for anything at the time it was used.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given to a זונה, which may not be brought as a קרבן
She went first; she acted before something else happened
She offered it as a קרבן

phrases.english: Where she first went ahead and sacrificed it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אלעזר's answer that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lamb given as payment is permitted if she offered it before the ביאה.

steps.title: If he gave it to her right away, the ruling is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבי אלעזר means. If the man gave her the lamb immediately, it is obviously permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he gave her full ownership of the lamb right away, then it is obvious that it is permitted, since up to that point he had not yet had a ביאה with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts testing רבי אלעזר's case by asking what exactly happened. It rules out the first option because that case would be too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lamb became hers immediately and she offered it, it was simply her own animal. No ביאה had happened yet, so it was never payment. A teaching that obvious would not need to be stated, so רבי אלעזר must mean some other case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
He gave her ownership of it
Immediately, right away
It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say that he transferred it to her immediately,
it is obvious that it is permitted,
since up to that point he had not yet had intercourse with her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 1 by asking what case it describes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's case of 'she offered it first'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ownership passed to her right away, the ruling is too obvious to need saying.

steps.title: If it only becomes hers at the ביאה, she cannot offer it
steps.stepSummary: The other option fails too. If the lamb is not hers until the ביאה, she cannot make it holy beforehand, because a person can only make holy what he owns.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he told her, 'It will not be yours until the time of the ביאה,' can she offer it? The תורה says, 'When a man makes his house holy to ה',' to teach that just as his house is his, everything one makes holy must be his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the opposite case and shows that it does not work either. Now רבי אלעזר's case seems impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule comes from the פסוק about making one's house holy: you can only make something הקדש if it is yours. Here the lamb does not belong to her before the ביאה, so she has no power to offer it then. That leaves no workable case for רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather (trying the other option)
The time of the ביאה
Is she able to? Can she?
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
In his ownership

phrases.english: But rather, where he said to her:
'It will not be acquired by you until the time of intercourse,'
can she sacrifice it?

phrases.aramaic: ״אִישׁ כִּי יַקְדִּישׁ אֶת בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳״
phrases.english: 'When a man sanctifies his house to be holy to the Lord'
the Merciful One said,
just as his house is in his possession,
so too anything he sanctifies must be in his possession!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the other option for the case and rejects it as well.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case where the lamb becomes hers only at the ביאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person cannot make something holy unless it is his, and the lamb is not yet hers.

steps.title: The answer: a mixed transfer of ownership
steps.stepSummary: The case is where he said the lamb becomes hers at the ביאה, but if she needs it sooner, it is hers from now.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is where he told her: 'It will be yours at the time of the ביאה, but if you need it, it is yours from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both challenges with a middle case. In this case the ruling is not obvious, and she still owned the lamb when she offered it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His main intent is that the lamb be payment for the ביאה, so you might think it counts as אתנן. Because of the clause 'if you need it, it is yours from now,' she owned it when she offered it. רבי אלעזר teaches that since it was offered before the ביאה, it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case
It will be acquired
You need it
From now

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's case works only with the double condition: hers at the ביאה, but hers right now if she needs it. That makes the case not obvious, and it also lets her own the lamb in time to offer it.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where he said to her:
'It will not be acquired by you until the time of intercourse,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'acquired.'

phrases.english: but if you need it,
let it be acquired by you from now.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both challenges from steps 2 and 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either the lamb was hers right away (obvious) or only at the ביאה (she could not offer it).
steps.terutzMaskana: A conditional transfer: hers at the ביאה, but hers from now if she needs it.

steps.title: What if she only made it holy first?
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא asks about a case where she made the lamb הקדש before the ביאה but did not offer it yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא asked: if she first made it הקדש, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב אושעיא wants to know whether making the lamb הקדש before the ביאה is enough to save it, or whether it must actually be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she offers it, the lamb is gone before the ביאה. When she only makes it הקדש, the lamb still exists at the time of the ביאה. The question is whether it can still become אתנן at that point.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question that has no clear answer yet
She made it הקדש (holy)
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya asked:
If she first consecrated it, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אלעזר's case and asks about a weaker version of it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does making the lamb הקדש before the ביאה protect it from becoming אתנן?

steps.title: Trying to answer from רבי אלעזר's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests answering from רבי אלעזר: he said 'offered,' which implies a lamb that was only made הקדש is אסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Answer it from רבי אלעזר, who said, 'She first offered it.' Only when she offered it is it permitted, because it no longer exists at the time of the ביאה. But if she only made it הקדש, it is אסור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רב אושעיא's question by reading closely what רבי אלעזר chose to say. This is a suggested proof, not yet a final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר specifically said 'offered.' The reason it is permitted is that the lamb is gone by the time of the ביאה. If she only made it הקדש, the lamb is still around at the ביאה, so it would still become אתנן and be אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolve (the question)
It does not exist; it is not there
Forbidden (here: forbidden for the מזבח)

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggested proof from the wording of רבי אלעזר. Do not treat it as the final halacha; the next step rejects this proof.

phrases.english: Resolve it from רבי אלעזר,
as רבי אלעזר said:
She first sacrificed it.
It is when she sacrificed it [that it is permitted],
since it does not exist at the time of intercourse,
but if she only consecrated it, it is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to רב אושעיא's question in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That a lamb only made הקדש before the ביאה is אסור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exact wording of רבי אלעזר: 'she first offered it,' not 'made it holy'

steps.title: The inference from רבי אלעזר is the very thing being asked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רב אושעיא's question is exactly whether we may draw that inference from רבי אלעזר, so his words cannot settle it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This itself is what he is asking: when she offered it, so the lamb no longer exists at the time of the ביאה, it is permitted. But if she only made it holy, then at the time of the ביאה it is forbidden. Is that right?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 6. Reading רבי אלעזר as forbidding a lamb that was only made holy is exactly what רב אושעיא is unsure about. Here the גמרא lays out the first side of his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 tried to prove from the word 'offered' that a lamb only made holy is forbidden. The גמרא answers that רב אושעיא already saw this reading and was asking whether it is correct. The first side reads: once the lamb is offered it is gone and there is nothing left to forbid, but a lamb that is only holy still exists at the ביאה and would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: This very point is what he is asking about
She offered it (brought it as a קרבן)
She made it holy (declared it הקדש)
It is not there / no longer exists

phrases.english: This itself is what he is asking about:
if she offered it, since it no longer exists at the time of the ביאה, it is permitted,
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'and it is not there' (round brackets). The corrected wording in square brackets says 'since it is not there.'

phrases.english: but if she only made it holy, then at the time of the ביאה it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 6 and begins laying out רב אושעיא's question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The attempt to settle רב אושעיא's question from the wording of רבי אלעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the very inference that רב אושעיא was unsure about, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: The other side: making it holy works like handing it over
steps.stepSummary: Maybe a lamb that was only made holy is also permitted. Saying 'this is for הקדש' is like handing the lamb to a person, so it left her ownership before the ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps, since we learned that 'saying something is for the Most High is like handing it over to an ordinary person,' if she made it holy it is permitted, and all the more so if she offered it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of רב אושעיא's question. Maybe making the lamb holy already takes it out of her hands, so it is permitted just like an offered lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה teaches that words of הקדש transfer ownership to Heaven as strongly as physically handing an item to a person. If so, once she declared it holy it was no longer hers at the ביאה, so it should be permitted. An offered lamb is then permitted all the more, which is why רבי אלעזר's word 'offered' may not be exact.

keyTerms.meaning: Saying an item is for הקדש is like handing it over to an ordinary person
The Most High (הקדש / the Temple)
An ordinary person
All the more so
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

phrases.english: Or perhaps, since we learned in a משנה:
'His saying something is for the Most High is like his handing it over to an ordinary person,'
phrases.notes: קידושין כח:. Just saying 'this is הקדש' moves ownership right away.

phrases.english: so if she made it holy, it is permitted,
and all the more so if she offered it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question whose first side was stated in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a lamb that was only made holy before the ביאה permitted, because הקדש works like a full transfer of ownership?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so רב אושעיא's question is left open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion without deciding. We do not know whether a lamb that was only made holy before the ביאה is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides have reasons behind them, and no source settles the question. The case of a lamb made holy but not yet offered stays in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: An offered lamb is clearly permitted. Whether a lamb that was only made holy is permitted is a תיקו, because we do not know if the words of הקדש alone took it out of her ownership.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the two-sided question from steps 7–8 without a decision.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a lamb made holy before the ביאה but not yet offered is permitted stays unresolved.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about payment given after the ביאה
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says payment given after the ביאה is permitted. Another says it is forbidden even if given twelve months later.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had relations with her and afterward gave her payment, her payment is permitted. But it was taught: if he had relations with her and gave her payment, even up to twelve months later, her payment is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא it has been studying and sets it against another ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא treats payment given after the ביאה as not real אתנן, so it may go on the מזבח. The second ברייתא calls it אתנן and forbids it, even after a long delay. The same case seems to get two opposite rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given to a זונה, which may not be brought on the מזבח
He had relations with her
Twelve months

phrases.english: If he had relations with her and afterward
gave her payment, her payment is permitted,
but wasn't it taught: if he had relations with her and then gave her,
and even if it was up to twelve months later,
her payment is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָתַן לָהּ אֶתְנַנָּה — מוּתָּר, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a later line in the ברייתא is shown to conflict with another ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that payment given after the ביאה is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא rules that payment given after the ביאה is forbidden, even twelve months later, which is a direct contradiction.

steps.title: A specific lamb versus an unspecified lamb
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רב חסדא explains that each ברייתא speaks about a different promise. A promised specific lamb is forbidden. An unspecified lamb is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רב חסדא said: There is no difficulty. This ברייתא is where he told her, 'Have relations with me for this lamb.' That ברייתא is where he told her, 'Have relations with me for a lamb,' without saying which one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 10 by showing that the two ברייתות are talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he pointed to a specific lamb before the ביאה, that lamb becomes her payment at the ביאה itself. It is forbidden even if he hands it over a year later. If he only promised 'a lamb' in general, no lamb was her payment at the time of the ביאה, so the one he gives her later is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: the two sources fit different cases
Have relations with me
This (specific) lamb
Without specifying

steps.whatToRemember: Payment given after the ביאה is forbidden if a specific lamb was promised beforehand, since it became hers at the ביאה. It is permitted if only an unspecified lamb was promised.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Rav Chisda said:
It is not difficult. This one is where he said to her:
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the second ברייתא, the one that forbids the payment.

phrases.english: 'Have relations with me for this lamb,'
that one is where he said to her:
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the first ברייתא, the one that permits the payment.

phrases.english: 'Have relations with me for a lamb,' without specifying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא refers to a different kind of promise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to rule on the same case of payment given after the ביאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A promised specific lamb is אתנן and forbidden even if given much later. An unspecified lamb given later is permitted.

steps.title: How can 'this lamb' be hers without pulling it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling that a promised specific lamb is forbidden: she never did משיכה, so she never acquired it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This lamb' is forbidden? But it is missing the act of pulling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 11 that a specific promised lamb ('this lamb') is forbidden as אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something is only אתנן if it actually became the woman's payment. Normally a person acquires an animal through משיכה, pulling it. Here she never pulled it, so how did it become hers and become forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: Missing the act of pulling, so the animal was never acquired
Pulling an object or animal toward oneself, a way of acquiring it

phrases.english: 'This lamb'
But it is missing pulling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case described in רב חנן בר רב חסדא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a specific promised lamb is forbidden as אתנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without משיכה she never acquired the lamb, so it was never really her payment.

steps.title: The case is a non-Jewish prostitute
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a גויה, who does not acquire through משיכה, so lacking משיכה is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a non-Jewish prostitute, who does not acquire through pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a non-Jewish woman, for whom pulling is not the way of acquiring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed she had to acquire the lamb by משיכה. For a גויה that is not her way of acquiring, so missing משיכה does not stop the lamb from becoming her payment.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish prostitute
She acquires

phrases.english: With a non-Jewish prostitute,
who does not acquire by pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a specific type of woman.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every woman must do משיכה to acquire the lamb.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a גויה, משיכה is not needed, so the lamb can be hers.

steps.title: Or a Jewish woman, with the lamb in her courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even a Jewish woman can acquire the lamb if it is standing in her courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: even a Jewish prostitute, for example when the lamb is standing in her courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer that works even for a Jewish woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's courtyard can acquire things for her, even without pulling. So if the lamb is standing in her חצר, she owns it without משיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces a second answer)
A Jewish prostitute
Her courtyard, which can acquire things for her

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
even with a Jewish prostitute,
such as where it stands in her courtyard.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the lamb. Her courtyard acquires it for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same קשיא in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative אוקימתא through acquisition by חצר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a גויה could own the lamb without pulling.
steps.terutzMaskana: A Jewish woman can also own it, through her courtyard.

steps.title: Then he gave it to her at the start
steps.stepSummary: If the lamb was in her courtyard, she owned it from the beginning, so it was not 'given after' the ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then he gave it to her from the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the courtyard answer: if the lamb was already in her courtyard, it became hers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke about a lamb given later, even twelve months later. If the lamb sat in her courtyard, she acquired it before the ביאה. So the case no longer matches the ברייתא's case of giving it afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: From the beginning

phrases.english: But he gave it to her from the beginning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Acquiring through her courtyard happens at once, which does not fit a ברייתא about payment given later.

steps.title: The lamb was a conditional pledge
steps.stepSummary: He set the lamb aside as an אפותיקי: if he pays money by a set day, fine; if not, the lamb is her payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he made it a designated pledge for her, and said to her: 'If by such-and-such a day I give you money, good. And if not, the lamb is your payment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the lamb was placed with her only as a backup payment, with a deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamb sits in her courtyard as a pledge, but it only becomes her payment if he fails to pay money by the deadline. So it truly becomes her payment later. Since it was a specific lamb promised for the ביאה, it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A designated pledge set aside to back up a payment
Good, fine
Your payment (as a prostitute)

steps.whatToRemember: A lamb set aside as a pledge, which becomes her payment only if he does not pay money, is still אתנן when it finally becomes hers.

phrases.english: Where he made it a pledge for her,
and said to her:
'If by such-and-such a day
I give you money, good,
and if not, the lamb is your payment.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case as a conditional pledge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A lamb in her courtyard must be hers from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: It stays a pledge and only becomes her payment later, if he does not pay money.

steps.title: Payment for any forbidden relationship is אתנן, except to one's wife who is a נדה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that payment for relations with a male, or with any of the עריות, is forbidden as אתנן, except payment to one's own wife who is a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Both payment for relations with a male and payment for relations with any of the forbidden women are forbidden, except payment to one's own wife who is a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: which kinds of payment count as אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב widens אתנן beyond a regular prostitute. It also covers payment for relations with a male and with any ערוה. He makes one exception: payment to his own wife while she is a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given for relations with a male
Forbidden sexual relationships
His wife while she is a נדה (in her menstrual period)
Except for

phrases.english: רב said:
Both the payment for a male,
and the payment for all forbidden relations,
are forbidden,
except for payment to his wife who is a נדה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the definition of אתנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment for relations with a male or any ערוה is אתנן and forbidden on the מזבח. Payment to one's wife who is a נדה is permitted.

steps.title: Why is the wife who is a נדה different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why payment to one's wife who is a נדה is not forbidden. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with a נדה are also forbidden, just like the other עריות. So the גמרא wants to know why this case alone is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רב's exception.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why payment to one's wife who is a נדה is not אתנן.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'prostitute', and his wife is not one
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק speaks of a זונה, and a man's own wife is not a זונה, even while she is a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Prostitute' is written, and this woman is not a prostitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק about אתנן uses the word זונה, which does not describe his own wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition is tied to the word זונה in the פסוק. The other forbidden women are counted as זונה in this sense. His own wife stays his wife even during נדה, so she is not a זונה and her payment is not אתנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A prostitute; the word the פסוק uses for אתנן
It is written

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, אתנן depends on the woman being a זונה, so payment to one's own wife is not אתנן, even while she is a נדה. לוי disagrees in the next step.

phrases.english: 'Prostitute' is written,
and this one is not a prostitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק forbids the payment of a זונה, and one's wife who is a נדה is not a זונה.

steps.title: Levi forbids even payment to one's wife who is a נדה
steps.stepSummary: לוי argues on רב: even payment to one's own wife who is a נדה is אתנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי said: even payment to his wife who is a נדה is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings לוי, who argues with רב's exception from the previous steps. For לוי, payment to one's own wife who is a נדה is also forbidden as אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had said a wife who is a נדה is not a זונה, so her payment is allowed. לוי removes that exception, so the prohibition covers every forbidden relationship, even with one's own wife.

keyTerms.meaning: His own wife while she is a נדה (forbidden to him for now)
Payment given for forbidden relations, which may not be brought on the מזבח

phrases.english: And Levi said: even his wife who is a menstruant.
phrases.notes: He means even payment to her is forbidden as אתנן, the opposite of רב's exception.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opinion that argues against רב's exception from steps 17-19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment to one's own wife who is a נדה is also forbidden as אתנן.

steps.title: Asking for Levi's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why לוי includes a wife who is a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for לוי's source. This sets up the next step, which gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב based himself on the word זונה, so the גמרא wants to know which word in the פסוק לוי relies on to include one's own wife.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of לוי's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which word in the פסוק לוי uses to include a wife who is a נדה.

steps.title: The פסוק says תועבה, and this is a תועבה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls אתנן a תועבה, and relations with a wife who is a נדה are also called תועבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Abomination' is written, and this is also an abomination.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives לוי's reason. The אתנן פסוק uses the word תועבה, and the תורה also calls relations with a נדה a תועבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי focuses on the word תועבה, not on זונה. Since every forbidden relationship, including with one's own wife who is a נדה, is called a תועבה, all such payments are included.

keyTerms.meaning: Abomination, the word the Torah uses for אתנן and also for forbidden relations

phrases.english: 'Abomination' is written,
phrases.notes: The אתנן פסוק (דברים 23:19) ends by calling it an abomination.

phrases.english: and this is an abomination.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:29 calls all the forbidden relations, a נדה included, 'abominations.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about לוי's reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word תועבה in the פסוק includes every forbidden relationship, even with one's own wife who is a נדה.

steps.title: But the פסוק says זונה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges לוי: the פסוק says זונה, and a wife is not a זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for לוי too, isn't it written 'זונה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges לוי with רב's word. The פסוק itself says זונה, so how can לוי include one's own wife?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זונה seems to limit אתנן to a woman who is not one's wife. If לוי ignores this limit, he must explain what the word זונה is there for.

keyTerms.meaning: A female prostitute
But isn't it written?

phrases.english: And Levi too,
but isn't it written 'prostitute'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges לוי using the word רב relied on in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's ruling that a wife who is a נדה is included.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word זונה should exclude one's own wife, as רב said, so לוי seems to ignore part of the פסוק.

steps.title: Levi: זונה excludes a male
steps.stepSummary: לוי uses the word זונה to teach that it applies to a female, not a male prostitute.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: that word teaches 'a female prostitute, and not a male prostitute.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for לוי. He uses the word זונה for a different purpose: to teach that the law applies only when a woman is paid, not when a man is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the word זונה teaches something. רב uses it to exclude one's own wife. לוי uses it to exclude a male who is paid, so for him the word does not exclude a wife.

keyTerms.meaning: A male prostitute
He would say to you (the גמרא answers for him)

phrases.english: He would say to you:
That word teaches 'a female prostitute,' and not a male prostitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: הָהִיא זוֹנָה, וְלֹא זוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against לוי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the word to teach something else
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word זונה must exclude one's own wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: For לוי, the word זונה excludes payment to a man, not payment to a wife.

steps.title: Where does רב learn 'female, not male'?
steps.stepSummary: If רב uses זונה for the wife, where does he learn that payment to a man is permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב, where does he learn 'female, and not male'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רב. רב used the word זונה up for the wife who is a נדה, so where does he learn that payment to a man is allowed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זונה cannot teach both rules for רב. The גמרא asks whether רב agrees with the male rule and, if so, what his source is.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he learn it?

phrases.english: And Rav,

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא זוֹנָה וְלֹא זוֹנֶה מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: that rule of 'female and not male,' from where does he learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב, הָהִיא זוֹנָה וְלֹא זוֹנֶה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב and asks for his source for לוי's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רב's source that payment to a male is not אתנן.

steps.title: רב learns it from רבי's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי teaches that only payment for a forbidden union is אתנן. Payment to a wife who is a נדה, a fee for lost work, and a woman paying a man are all permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from רבי, as it is taught: רבי says, the only forbidden אתנן is payment to any of the עריות who are forbidden to him. But payment to his wife who is a נדה, a fee he gave her for her lost time, and payment she gave him are all permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב learns the male rule from a ברייתא of רבי. It lists three payments that are permitted, and the last one is a woman paying a man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי limits אתנן to payment for a union that is a real sin with no permitted side. That leaves out one's own wife who is a נדה, which matches רב. It also leaves out a fee for her lost work, and payment going from the woman to the man, which gives רב his source for 'not male.'

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden relations
Through a sin, a union that is forbidden
For her loss, a fee for the work time she gave up
Permitted (to be brought on the מזבח)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא supports רב's exception for one's own wife, and it gives a source for the male rule without using the word זונה.

phrases.english: He derives it from Rabbi,
as it is taught: Rabbi says:
No payment is forbidden
except payment to any of the forbidden women
phrases.notes: The corrected wording leaves out the word in round brackets and adds the words in square brackets.

phrases.english: who come to him through a sin,
but payment to his wife who is a menstruant,
and what he gave her as a fee for her lost time,
and what she gave him as his payment, are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers where רב learns the male rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב learns it from רבי's ברייתא, which permits payment that a woman gives to a man.

steps.title: A hint from יחזקאל: a woman who pays is the reverse
steps.stepSummary: רבי brings a hint, not a proof, from a פסוק in יחזקאל that a woman paying a man is the reverse of אתנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is no proof for this, there is a hint: 'And in that you gave payment, and no payment is given to you, you are the reverse.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ends with a hint from נביא for his last case. When a woman pays the man, the פסוק calls it 'the reverse,' so it is not normal אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words of נביא cannot serve as a real source for a Torah law, so רבי calls it only a hint. The hint still fits his rule: אתנן is payment given to the woman, not payment from her.

keyTerms.meaning: A hint for the matter, weaker than a full proof
Proof
The reverse, the opposite

steps.whatToRemember: רב: a wife who is a נדה is not a זונה, so her payment is permitted, and the male rule comes from רבי. לוי: everything called תועבה is included, even one's own wife, and the word זונה only excludes a male.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: Even though there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint for the matter:
'And in that you gave payment,'
and no payment is given to you,
phrases.notes: The corrected wording reads 'to you' (square brackets) instead of 'to her' (round brackets).

phrases.english: thus you are the reverse.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר, זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי's last case with a hint from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's ruling that payment from a woman to a man is not אתנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 16:34, which calls a woman paying a man 'the reverse.'

steps.title: What does רב do with the word 'abomination'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב uses the word תועבה, since he did not learn לוי's rule from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב, what does he do with this word 'abomination'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רב learns from the word תועבה in the פסוק about אתנן. This question sets up the next step, where the גמרא gives רב a different use for the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי used תועבה to teach that payment to a נדה wife counts as אתנן. רב disagrees with that rule, so the word seems to have no job in his view. The גמרא assumes every word in the תורה teaches something, so it asks what רב does with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Abomination. A word in the פסוק about אתנן (דברים 23:19).
What does he do with it? The גמרא's standard way of asking how someone uses a word that he did not use for the other opinion's rule.

phrases.english: And רב, this word "abomination"
what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא has explained where רב learns his rules. Now it asks what the extra word תועבה teaches in his view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רב learns from the word תועבה, since he does not use it for לוי's rule.

steps.title: רב needs the word for אביי's rule about a gentile prostitute
steps.stepSummary: רב uses תועבה for אביי's rule that a gentile prostitute's payment is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what אביי said. אביי said: a gentile prostitute's payment is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב uses the word תועבה to teach אביי's rule: payment to a non-Jewish prostitute counts as forbidden אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the word has a job in רב's view. It is not about a wife who is a נדה. It tells us which kind of woman's payment is forbidden, and the next step explains how.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish prostitute.
Her payment, the fee given for the forbidden relations.
He needs it. The word is used for a different teaching.

phrases.english: He needs it for what אביי said,
as אביי said:
A gentile prostitute: her payment is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב uses תועבה for אביי's rule that a gentile prostitute's payment is forbidden as אתנן.

steps.title: The source: a word link between 'abomination' and forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: אביי links תועבה here to תועבות in the עריות section, so אתנן applies to a woman with whom קידושין cannot take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Here it says 'abomination,' and there it says 'For whoever does any of these abominations.' Just as there it means forbidden relations, with whom קידושין do not take effect, so too here it means a woman with whom קידושין do not take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how אביי learns his rule. The same word, תועבה, appears both in the אתנן פסוק and in the list of עריות, and that shared word links the two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עריות are relationships where קידושין cannot take effect at all. Because of the link, אתנן also applies only to a woman with whom קידושין cannot take effect. A gentile woman fits this, since a Jew's קידושין do not take effect with her, so her payment is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here, and it is written there. This is how a גזרה שוה (a link between two פסוקים through a shared word) is introduced.
Forbidden relationships listed in ויקרא 18.
Betrothal takes effect, meaning a valid marriage bond can be created.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up: אביי does not say every act of זנות makes the payment forbidden. The test is whether קידושין could take effect with this woman.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is written here "abomination,"
and it is written there:

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי כׇּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה מִכֹּל הַתּוֹעֵבוֹת הָאֵל״,
phrases.english: "For whoever shall do any of these abominations,"
just as there it is forbidden relations,
with whom betrothal does not take effect,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי אֵין קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בָּהּ.
phrases.english: so too here it is one with whom betrothal does not take effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? כְּתִיב הָכָא ״תּוֹעֵבָה״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for אביי's rule from step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That payment to a gentile prostitute is forbidden אתנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזרה שוה linking תועבה (דברים 23:19) with התועבות (ויקרא 18:29): both refer to women with whom קידושין do not take effect.

steps.title: A כהן is not lashed for a gentile prostitute
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that a כהן who has relations with a gentile זונה is not lashed for the איסור of זונה, because her children are not counted after him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a כהן who had relations with her is not lashed because of the איסור of זונה. Why? The פסוק says 'he shall not profane his seed.' That means one whose children are counted after him. This leaves out a gentile woman, whose children are not counted after him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second rule about the gentile זונה. A כהן is not lashed for the איסור of a זונה with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור for a כהן is tied to 'not profaning his seed.' That only applies when the child belongs to the father's line. A child born to a gentile mother follows the mother and is not a Jew, so it is not counted after the כהן, and the איסור does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Is lashed (gets מלקות).
He shall not profane his seed (ויקרא 21:15).
Counted after him. The child's family line goes after the father.
Excludes, leaves out.

phrases.english: And a כהן who had relations with her
is not lashed for her because of the איסור of a זונה,
phrases.notes: This is the איסור for a כהן to take a זונה, in ויקרא 21:7.

phrases.english: What is the reason? Because the פסוק says:
"He shall not profane his seed"
that is, one whose children are counted after him,
which leaves out a gentile woman,
whose children are not counted after him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹהֵן שֶׁבָּא עָלֶיהָ אֵין לוֹקֶה עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם זוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's statement with a second rule about the same gentile זונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who has relations with a gentile זונה is not lashed for the איסור of זונה, because the children are not counted after him.

steps.title: A Jewish prostitute is the reverse on both points
steps.stepSummary: With a Jewish זונה the payment is permitted, because קידושין take effect with her. A כהן is lashed for her, because the children are counted after him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jewish prostitute: her payment is permitted. Why? Because קידושין take effect with her. And a כהן who had relations with her is lashed because of the איסור of זונה. Why? Because the children are counted after him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes by showing that a Jewish זונה works the opposite way from a gentile one on both rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two tests from before decide each case. אתנן depends on whether קידושין can take effect, and with a Jewish woman they can, so the payment is permitted. The כהן's איסור depends on whether the children are counted after him, and here they are, so he is lashed.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish prostitute.
Permitted.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי uses two different tests. For אתנן: can קידושין take effect with her? (Gentile: no, so the payment is forbidden. Jewish: yes, so it is permitted.) For a כהן: are the children counted after him? (Gentile: no, so no lashes. Jewish: yes, so he is lashed.) This is how רב uses the word תועבה.

phrases.english: A Jewish prostitute:
her payment is permitted. What is the reason?
Because betrothal takes effect with her.
And a כהן who had relations with her
is lashed because of the איסור of a זונה. What is the reason?
Because his children are counted after him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the opposite case to steps 29 to 31, using the same two tests.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jewish זונה's payment is permitted, and a כהן who has relations with her is lashed.

steps.title: רבא: Gentile and Jewish prostitutes are treated the same
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי. For both a gentile זונה and a Jewish זונה, the אתנן is forbidden, and a כהן is lashed for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא says: For both this one and that one, her payment is forbidden, and a כהן who has relations with her is lashed because of the איסור of זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own opinion, which goes against אביי's two rules from the last steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי split the cases: a gentile זונה has forbidden אתנן but no lashes, and a Jewish זונה has permitted אתנן but lashes. רבא makes both cases equal on both points: the אתנן is forbidden and the כהן gets lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: A prostitute's payment, which may not be brought as a קרבן
Is lashed (gets מלקות)
Because of the איסור for a כהן to be with a זונה

phrases.english: And Rava says:
Both this one and that one,
phrases.notes: He means both the gentile זונה and the Jewish זונה from אביי's two rules.

phrases.english: her payment is forbidden,
and a priest who has relations with her
is lashed because of the prohibition of a prostitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes אביי's rules in steps 31-32
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For both a gentile and a Jewish זונה, the אתנן is forbidden and a כהן is lashed.

steps.title: רבא's reason: Each case learns from the other
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the two cases teach each other. The Jewish זונה passes her לאו to the gentile, and the gentile passes her forbidden אתנן to the Jewish one.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? They are learned from each other. Just as a Jewish זונה is forbidden to a כהן by a לאו, so too a gentile זונה is forbidden by a לאו. And just as a gentile זונה's payment is forbidden, so too a Jewish זונה's payment is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רבא's opinion: each case lends its rule to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case starts out with one clear rule. The Jewish זונה clearly has a לאו for a כהן, and the gentile זונה clearly has forbidden אתנן (from אביי's own source). רבא swaps them, so both cases end up with both rules.

keyTerms.meaning: They are learned from each other
Forbidden by a negative commandment (a לאו)
A gentile prostitute

phrases.english: What is the reason?
They are learned from one another:
Just as a Jewish prostitute is under a prohibition,
so too a gentile prostitute is under a prohibition,
and just as a gentile prostitute's payment is forbidden,
so too a Jewish prostitute's payment is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבא's ruling
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that both cases are equal
steps.raayaSupportSource: A two-way comparison between the two kinds of זונה

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to refute אביי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the אתנן of both a gentile and a Jewish זונה is forbidden. That goes against אביי, who permitted the Jewish זונה's payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: For both a gentile זונה and a Jewish זונה, her payment is forbidden. This is a refutation of אביי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to prove אביי wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said a Jewish זונה's אתנן is permitted, because קידושין take effect with her. The ברייתא forbids both, which matches רבא and seems to knock out אביי completely.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: a source that seems to prove an opinion wrong
A Jewish prostitute

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Both a gentile prostitute
and a Jewish prostitute:
her payment is forbidden.
This is a refutation of Abaye!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אֶחָד זוֹנָה גּוֹיָה וְאֶחָד זוֹנָה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a ברייתא to attack אביי's rule from step 32
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that a Jewish זונה's אתנן is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids the אתנן of a Jewish זונה, which directly goes against אביי.

steps.title: אביי: The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that קידושין do not take effect with חייבי לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי could say to you: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי עקיבא, who said that קידושין do not take effect with חייבי לאוין.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself by saying which תנא the ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's test is whether קידושין can take effect with the woman. For רבי עקיבא, a woman forbidden by a לאו cannot have קידושין take effect. So her אתנן is forbidden even under אביי's own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
Betrothal takes effect
Relationships forbidden by a regular לאו

phrases.english: Abaye could say to you:
Whose opinion is this?
It is Rabbi Akiva,
who said: Betrothal does not take effect
with those liable for prohibitions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ אַבָּיֵי: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תיובתא of step 35
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ברייתא to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids every Jewish זונה's אתנן, against אביי
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, for whom קידושין don't take effect with חייבי לאוין, so it fits אביי's test

steps.title: What the ברייתא teaches, according to אביי
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, the ברייתא teaches that any זונה with whom קידושין cannot take effect has forbidden אתנן, like the widow with a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what it teaches us: any זונה with whom קידושין cannot take effect is like an אלמנה, with whom קידושין cannot take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's answer by explaining what the ברייתא means in his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'Jewish זונה' in the ברייתא is a woman with whom קידושין cannot take effect, like an אלמנה with a כהן גדול according to רבי עקיבא. So the ברייתא is not talking about every Jewish זונה, and אביי's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us
Similar to, like
A widow, who is forbidden to a כהן גדול

steps.whatToRemember: For אביי, the ברייתא's Jewish זונה is only one with whom קידושין cannot take effect (according to רבי עקיבא), so his rule survives.

phrases.english: And this teaches us

phrases.aramaic: דְּכׇל זוֹנָה לָא תָּפְסִי בַּהּ קִדּוּשִׁין,
phrases.english: that every prostitute with whom betrothal does not take effect
is like a widow
with whom betrothal does not take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by reading the ברייתא's example
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the ברייתא as speaking about women with whom קידושין cannot take effect
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's example of a widow shows it only means a זונה with whom קידושין cannot take effect

steps.title: For רבא, why mention the widow with a כהן גדול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבא, why does the ברייתא choose the example of a widow with a כהן גדול?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא, what is different that it teaches 'for example, a widow with a כהן גדול'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to רבא and challenges him with the widow example in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the widow example makes sense, because קידושין cannot take effect with her. For רבא, even an ordinary Jewish זונה has forbidden אתנן, so the special example of a widow seems unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this case specifically?
For example
The High Priest, who may not marry a widow

phrases.english: And according to Rava,
what is different that it teaches:
"For example, a widow with a High Priest"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending אביי, the גמרא now challenges רבא with the same ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that every Jewish זונה's אתנן is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every זונה's אתנן is forbidden, the ברייתא's specific example of a widow with a כהן גדול seems pointless.

steps.title: The widow example teaches that it must be clearly called payment
steps.stepSummary: For רבא, the widow example teaches a comparison. Lashes for the widow need a warning, and the payment only counts as אתנן if he says 'here, this is for you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like an אלמנה. Just as with an אלמנה there are no lashes until they are warned, so too with a זונה, it is not אתנן until he says, 'Here, this is for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבא: the widow example is there to teach a condition for when a payment counts as אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a widow and a כהן גדול, lashes need a התראה, a clear warning. In the same way, a gift only becomes אתנן when he clearly says it is payment for the relations ('הא לך'). So the example is not about קידושין at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They warn him (התראה), which is needed before lashes
Here, this is for you: words that make the gift a payment

steps.whatToRemember: For אביי, the widow example shows 'no קידושין.' For רבא, it shows that the payment must be clearly given as payment, the way lashes need a clear warning.

phrases.english: It is like a widow:
just as with a widow there are no lashes
until they warn him,
so too with a prostitute,
not until he says, "Here, this is for you."
phrases.notes: The words left out here are 'it is not אתנן.' It only counts once he clearly hands it over as payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוּמְיָא דְּאַלְמָנָה — מָה אַלְמָנָה לָא לָקֵי עַד דְּמַתְרִי בֵּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on רבא from step 38
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the example a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The widow example only makes sense for the 'no קידושין' test
steps.terutzMaskana: The example teaches that, just as lashes need a warning, אתנן needs a clear statement of payment ('הא לך')

steps.title: רבא's rule excludes רבי אלעזר, but a woman who was already a prostitute is different
steps.stepSummary: רבא's requirement of 'here, this is for you' rejects רבי אלעזר, who holds that any relations outside marriage make a woman a זונה. Still, if she was a זונה from the start, her payment is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rejects the view of רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר said: an unmarried man who has relations with an unmarried woman, not for the sake of marriage, has made her a זונה. But where she was a זונה from the start, then her payment is indeed forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's answer from the last step. It explains which opinion his rule pushes away, and it adds one case where the payment is forbidden even without the special words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, a single encounter with a פנויה does not make her a זונה unless he says 'here, this is for you'. That rejects רבי אלעזר, who says any such encounter already makes her a זונה. The limit is a woman who was a זונה from the start: her payment is forbidden automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to reject another opinion
An unmarried man / an unmarried woman
For the sake of marriage
From the start; originally

phrases.english: This excludes the view of Rabbi Elazar,
for Rabbi Elazar said:
An unmarried man who has relations with an unmarried woman
not for the sake of marriage
has made her a prostitute.
But where she was a prostitute from the start,
then indeed it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's answer from step 39 by naming the opinion it rejects and adding a limit to it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the scope of the answer and adding a limit to it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think any relations outside marriage make a woman a זונה, as רבי אלעזר holds.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבא, a one-time encounter only counts as זנות if he says 'here, this is for you'. A woman who was already a זונה has forbidden payment anyway.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, a one-time encounter with a פנויה only creates אתנן with the words 'here, this is for you'. That rejects רבי אלעזר. A woman who was already a זונה has forbidden payment no matter what.

steps.title: Another version of אביי's answer: the ברייתא is about עריות, where קידושין cannot take effect
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, אביי answers that the ברייתא forbidding a Jewish זונה's payment is about עריות, where קידושין cannot take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: when the ברייתא teaches this, it is talking about עריות, where קידושין do not take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of how אביי answered the ברייתא from step 35. In this version, the ברייתא only forbids the payment in cases of עריות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, אביי limits the ברייתא to women with whom קידושין cannot take effect. That leaves his own ruling, which permits the payment, for a woman with whom קידושין can take effect. Steps 42–43 then test this limit against the end of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of how the discussion went
The most severe forbidden relations
Betrothal takes effect

phrases.english: Another version:
When that baraita teaches this,
it is talking about forbidden relations where betrothal does not take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different version of אביי's answer to the קשיא in step 35, in place of the answer in step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to forbid the payment of every Jewish זונה, which goes against אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only covers עריות, where קידושין cannot take effect. אביי's ruling covers women with whom קידושין can take effect.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is a second version of אביי's answer to the same ברייתא from step 35.

steps.title: But the ברייתא's last part lists cases where קידושין do take effect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version of אביי's answer. The end of the ברייתא forbids the payment of a widow with a כהן גדול and of a divorcee or חלוצה with a כהן הדיוט, and קידושין do take effect in those cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the last part of the ברייתא teaches: a widow with a כהן גדול, or a divorcee or חלוצה with a כהן הדיוט, her payment is forbidden. Yet with these women קידושין do take effect!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second version of אביי's answer by quoting the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי just said the ברייתא is only about women with whom קידושין cannot take effect. But the ברייתא's own examples are only regular prohibitions (חייבי לאוין), and קידושין do take effect with them. So the ברייתא forbids the payment even where קידושין work, and that does not fit this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a teaching
A woman who has done חליצה; she is forbidden to a כהן
An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול
The payment given to a זונה, which may not be brought as an offering

phrases.english: But it teaches in the last part:
a widow with a High Priest,
a divorcee or a ḥalutza with an ordinary priest:
her payment is forbidden.
But with these women, betrothal does take effect!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version of אביי's answer from step 41.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא only covers women with whom קידושין cannot take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own examples are cases where קידושין do take effect, so it cannot be limited to עריות.

steps.title: Whose opinion does this ברייתא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer by asking which תנא the ברייתא follows. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to answer the challenge by naming the תנא behind the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking 'whose opinion is this?' hints that the ברייתא follows a תנא who holds that קידושין do not take effect even with these women. If so, the widow and divorcee cases also count as cases where קידושין cannot take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? (used to bring in the answer)

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the challenge in step 42.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Naming the תנא behind the ברייתא (the answer continues on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to include cases where קידושין take effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer continues on the next amud, where the גמרא names the תנא whose view makes these cases fit.
